title: OAuth start trusts the incoming request host when building the callback URL

evidence.quote:
callback_url = str(request.url_for("oauth_web_callback"))
auth_url = service.get_auth_url(callback_url)
logger.info(f"OAuth flow started, callback URL: {callback_url}")
return RedirectResponse(url=auth_url)

reasoning: GET /oauth/start is intentionally unauthenticated and receives network-controlled request metadata. Building the OAuth redirect_uri from request.url_for means the value can depend on the incoming Host/proxy scheme rather than a configured public origin. In the best case this causes OAuth failures behind proxies or with spoofed Host headers; in weaker deployment configurations it can send users into a consent flow whose redirect_uri was influenced by an attacker-controlled request header.
reproduction: Send GET /oauth/start with a forged Host header and inspect the Location header returned by the endpoint; the generated Google authorization URL will be based on the request-derived callback URL.
recommendation: Build the OAuth callback URL from a trusted configured public base URL, or validate the request-derived origin against an allowlist before passing it to get_auth_url.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for /oauth/start, and the provided file does not show coverage for Host/proxy-derived callback URL behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test for GET /oauth/start that sends a forged Host header and asserts the redirect_uri uses the configured trusted public origin or rejects the request.
minimumFixScope: Update oauth_start to derive callback_url from trusted configuration or enforce allowed hosts/origins for this route.
